inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,085 normalized lines. The paper develops low-lying one-level density for large-weight GL2, large-level GL2, and symmetric-square GL3 families; isolates the beyond-diagonal Kloosterman/character-sum contributions that distinguish orthogonal parity types and symplectic symmetry; converts the density statements into central nonvanishing bounds; and solves the resulting band-limited extremal problem through a positive Fredholm operator. Formula extraction is imperfect but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from contiguous prose and displayed equations.

accepted_units.title: Three conductor-ordered families and their symmetry classes
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes large-weight GL2, large-level GL2, and symmetric-square GL3 families, then uses self-duality and functional-equation signs to predict O/SO parity types versus Sp.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the motivating function-field/monodromy viewpoint and the exact family definitions needed to interpret every later density statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose with light notation; the family and sign distinctions survive the imperfect text-layer rendering.

accepted_units.title: Scaled low-lying zero density as a symmetry observable
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the conductor-scaled one-level statistic and states the density conjecture that identifies its family limit with a random-matrix symmetry kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the zero parametrization, scale, averaging convention, four kernels, and conjecture together so the observable is not detached from its semantics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed formulas are text-layer fragmented, but the prose fixes the scale and the named kernels; scan verification would be prudent for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Density theorem across three families and why support past one matters
accepted_units.why_material: States the conditional support ranges for parity-split GL2 and symmetric-square densities and explains that crossing Fourier support one activates genuinely new Kloosterman off-diagonal main terms.
accepted_units.context_note: The remarks are essential: they distinguish diagonal confirmation from the stronger beyond-diagonal test of the symmetry conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem equations are recoverable by surrounding family labels and prose; exact interval endpoints should remain tied to the displayed text.

accepted_units.title: Positive band-limited tests convert density into central nonvanishing
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces constrained positive test-function optimization, states the resulting nonvanishing and mean-rank-style bounds, and explains that support extension is what beats diagonal-only thresholds.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes limitations and comparison remarks, including the dependence on GRH and the modular-Jacobian application.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fractions and central-point typography are noisy, but the numbered cases and explanatory prose make the mechanism and direction of bounds recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Prime exponential-sum cancellation would force a GL2 zero-free region
accepted_units.why_material: Pairs an unconditional parity-mixed weighted density with a stronger prime-progressions hypothesis, then derives extended support and a quasi-Riemann-hypothesis consequence for large-weight GL2 forms.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit captures the source's explicit bridge from a classical GL1-type cancellation statement to control of GL2 zeros, including the stated auxiliary zero-location assumption.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponential-sum display and numerical endpoint are legible enough in context, though exact formula reuse should be checked against the page image.

accepted_units.title: Bessel summation, Petersson averaging, and the explicit formula
accepted_units.why_material: Assembles the three transformations used repeatedly: averaging Bessel kernels over weight, replacing form averages by diagonal plus Kloosterman sums, and replacing zeros by prime-power coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records why inverse symmetric-square values are the natural Petersson weights and how the sign-restricted averaging operators are normalized.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy and text-layer fragile; the roles of each proposition are secure from prose, but exact kernels and constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Explicit-formula decomposition in the diagonal support regime
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how the zero statistic splits into archimedean, prime-square, prime, and higher terms; compact support bounds prime ranges so Petersson plus Weil makes the non-diagonal pieces negligible and leaves the O-density main term.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is useful as a baseline against which every later support-extension contribution is identified.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed summands are OCR-sensitive, but their named decomposition and the support-to-prime-range logic are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Extended support turns density positivity into individual zero exclusion
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks the new oscillatory Bessel term past the diagonal range, controls it by the prime-progressions hypothesis, and uses a nonnegative squared-sinc test to turn the averaged estimate into a bound on each real off-line zero.
accepted_units.context_note: Preserves the chain from support restriction through the hyperbolic growth estimate to the stated zero-free endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The asymptotic inequalities contain extraction risk; the prose and equation sequence establish the argument, while exact exponent checking should use the scan.

accepted_units.title: Removing harmonic weights before parity-sensitive averaging
accepted_units.why_material: Uses GRH to approximate the symmetric-square value by a short Dirichlet series, multiplies it into the explicit formula, and separates diagonal, negligible, and potentially main off-diagonal pieces.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the critical unweighting step that makes uniform sign-restricted family counts comparable to harmonic Petersson averages.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dense; the short-series reduction and term classification are reliable from prose, but precise summation indices warrant scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Kloosterman-to-character conversion yields the SO parity split
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the surviving prime-linear Petersson term by Bessel averaging, character orthogonality, GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, and a principal-character main term, producing opposite Fourier-tail corrections for the two signs.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the final replacement of the fixed K-scale statistic by the true conductor-scaled density and therefore closes the large-weight theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and nested sums are text-layer sensitive; the off-diagonal pipeline and final SO(even)/SO(odd) interpretations are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Symmetric-square explicit formula and identification of its exceptional term
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the prime coefficients for symmetric squares, introduces the corresponding uniform average, and isolates the prime-square term that becomes a main term only beyond support one.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit includes the target symplectic density and the bounds that dispose of the other components.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The coefficient identity is formula-dependent; the surrounding prose clearly identifies which term is non-diagonal and why it matters.

accepted_units.title: Poisson analysis of the symmetric-square term produces symplectic density
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms the exceptional Petersson term into arithmetic sums, evaluates a multiplicative Kloosterman aggregate, applies Poisson summation, extracts the zero-frequency main term, and proves the remaining frequencies negligible.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with the Fourier correction and the completed support-4/3 symplectic density theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This long span is highly formula-dependent and should be scan-checked before exact reuse; the sequence of transformations and the main-versus-error distinction remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Large-level newform normalization and Petersson weights
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the level-N functional-equation sign, unfolds an Eisenstein series to identify the first Fourier coefficient and natural harmonic weight, then obtains usable Petersson estimates including a special coefficient involving N.
accepted_units.context_note: This setup explains why the later sign projector inserts a level-N Hecke eigenvalue rather than merely restricting a list of forms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many displayed normalizations are extraction-sensitive; the derivation path and proposition roles are coherent.

accepted_units.title: From harmonic level averages to uniform sign subfamilies
accepted_units.why_material: Defines uniform and sign-projected sums, removes the inverse symmetric-square harmonic weight with a short series, establishes equal leading sizes for the two signs, and states the level-aspect explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit is the large-level analogue of the large-weight unweighting step but with the functional-equation sign encoded through the Fricke/level coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator identities are legible, while exact error exponents and prime-term coefficients should be checked against the source image.

accepted_units.title: Large-level density isolates a single non-diagonal prime term
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the sign-restricted density average, evaluates the universal and prime-square pieces, and identifies the remaining prime-linear contribution as the only order-N source of symmetry separation beyond support one.
accepted_units.context_note: This concise reduction makes the subsequent lengthy character-sum argument conceptually navigable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Term labels and asymptotic roles are clear despite imperfect display extraction.

accepted_units.title: The parity-blind large-level off-diagonal term cancels
accepted_units.why_material: Applies Petersson, truncates the modulus, expands primes by residue-class characters, and uses Dirichlet GRH to show both principal and nonprincipal portions of the parity-blind contribution are lower order.
accepted_units.context_note: The negative result is structurally useful because it locates the actual density correction in the sign-weighted component.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested sums are OCR-fragile, but the split, character bound, and conclusion IVA=o(N) are explicit.

accepted_units.title: The level coefficient creates the orthogonal Fourier-tail correction
accepted_units.why_material: Inserts the functional-equation sign as a level-N coefficient, factors the Kloosterman sum, removes nonprincipal characters, and evaluates the principal contribution to obtain opposite tail terms and hence SO(even)/SO(odd) densities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the large-level causal mechanism for parity separation, not merely a repetition of the large-weight conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Kloosterman identities, Bessel integrals, and constants need scan verification; the sign-dependent structure and final kernels are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Nonconstant Fourier-side density makes the standard sinc test suboptimal
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the constrained nonnegative band-limited density infimum and observes that a nonconstant Fourier-side correction—created by off-diagonal analysis—prevents the familiar squared-sinc function from attaining it.
accepted_units.context_note: This bridges the analytic density theorem to the functional-analytic appendix.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual prose is clear; the infimum display is recoverable with minor formula-layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Density bounds, parity of vanishing, and strict nonvanishing gains
accepted_units.why_material: Uses positivity and parity of central vanishing order to turn extremal density values into explicit nonvanishing proportions, and shows why splitting signs gives a strict mean-order gain that the parity-mixed O-kernel cannot provide.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the analogous symmetric-square deduction and its dependence on support 4/3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several numerical fractions are visually degraded; the inequality logic is intact, but exact reported constants should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Band-limited positivity becomes a Fredholm quadratic minimization
accepted_units.why_material: Factors admissible positive test functions as squared entire functions, transfers the problem by Plancherel to a convolution quotient, and identifies the minimizer through the equation (I+K)f=1.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the singular-kernel alternative, positivity, compact self-adjoint structure, and uniqueness condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator argument is prose-supported; exact function spaces in one display show a likely extraction inconsistency and should be checked before formal transcription.

accepted_units.title: A projection argument characterizes when squared sinc is optimal
accepted_units.why_material: Proves the Fredholm minimizer by decomposing any normalized competitor into the solution plus an orthogonal remainder, then shows the constant Fourier factor—and hence squared sinc—is optimal exactly when the kernel average is constant.
accepted_units.context_note: Applying the criterion to SO(even), SO(odd), Sp, and O explains why only the parity-mixed orthogonal kernel retains the standard test.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The variational proof is robust in prose and notation; kernel indicator displays are legible.

accepted_units.title: Solving the symmetry-kernel Fredholm equations sharpens nonvanishing
accepted_units.why_material: Uses evenness to reduce the SO kernels to integral equations, solves them by trigonometric functions, and feeds the resulting minimum values back into improved nonvanishing and mean-order bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides a complete example of turning a qualitative non-optimality diagnosis into quantitative gains.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The trigonometric formulas and cotangent arguments are notably garbled in extraction; only the construction and printed decimals are safe without scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact accessible range and arithmetic evaluation differ by family, aspect, and hypotheses; this is a source-internal pattern, not a universal theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The two implementations are analogous but not identical, and both conclusions are conditional on the stated GRH assumptions and support ranges.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The resulting proportions are lower bounds under the source's hypotheses, not exact nonvanishing densities.
